newsitem.title: JAPAN: SOCCER-KASHIMA KEEPS TOP PLACE, FUKUOKA EARNS FIRST WIN.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-KASHIMA KEEPS TOP PLACE, FUKUOKA EARNS FIRST WIN.

text.p: Defending J.League champions Kashima Antlers remained unbeaten after holding off Jubilo Iwata 2-1 with a last-minute goal by Yasuo Manaka in Saturday's game.
Manaka scored from 20 meters away just before the final whistle in an evenly balanced match before a near-capacity crowd of 14,000.
Elsewhere, Avispa Fukuoka earned their first win of the season against Gamba Osaka 1-0 on Saturday in the absence of Gamba's key forward Patrick Mboma.
The Cameroonian forward was away for the World Cup, and Gamba Osaka, which led the league in the opening four rounds, tumbled to fifth place.
Yokohama Flugels scored their 2-0 home win over pre-season favorite Nagoya Grampus Eight after Brazilian Valber and Hiroki Hattori scored second-half goals.
Nagoya, which missed Yugoslav player Dragan Stojkovic, also away for World Cup duty, struggled as the only team yet to win a point.
Kashiwa Reysols beat J.League newcomer Vissel Kobe 3-1, while Sanfrecce Hiroshima won 2-1 and Shimizu S-Pulse notched a 3-1 win. Bellmare Hiratsuka was idle.
